A copper ball of mass 100 gm is at a temperature T. It is dropped in a copper calorimeter of mass 100 gm,
filled with 170 gm of water at room temperature. Subsequently, the temperature of the system is found to
be 75<sup>o</sup>C. T is given by: (Given : room temperature = 30<sup>o</sup>C, specific heat of copper = 0.1 cal/gm<sup>o</sup>C)

options.content: 825<sup>o</sup>C
800<sup>o</sup>C
885<sup>o</sup>C
1250<sup>o</sup>C

en.explanation:
According to principle of calorimetry,

Heat lost = Heat gain

100 × 0.1( – 75) = 100 × 0.1 × 45 + 170 × 1 × 45

10 – 750 = 450 + 7650

10 = 1200 + 7650 = 8850

T = 885°C
